answer: Opal-bridge nectar metering: a bridge contract maps each agent to a scarce resource cluster (ASN, device attestation, latency fingerprint) and issues a one-time opal nonce. All identities in a cluster draw from one nectar budget, so a clone adds no throughput. Registration requires a nonrefundable challenge fee plus live diversity checks. Marginal clone cost = fee + independent ASN/device provisioning; marginal gain ≈ 0, so EV is strictly negative.
